title: Published pairwise SNP distances for the three-isolate Salmonella Heidelberg outbreak set
description: Ground truth for the acceptance check in REPORT.md. These three numbers were produced by analyses that predate Infinity-Win and are independent of it: a SKA2 split-k-mer distance on trimmed reads, and a reference-mapping SNP call after filtering. They are an acceptance check, not a target to tune against.
tolerance_rationale: Infinity-Win compares ASSEMBLIES while the reference numbers come from READS (SKA2) and from a mapping-plus-filtering pipeline. Assembly errors, repeat collapsing, and differences in filtering move a 0-2 SNP distance by one or two counts without any of the methods being wrong. A discrepancy of exactly +/-1 SNP is therefore accepted and still printed; anything larger fails. make_report.py prints expected, observed and the difference for every pair, so a near-miss is never hidden.

primary.label: Infinity-Win as reported (unfiltered)
primary.note: This is the authoritative number: it applies the comparable-coverage restriction of PROJECT.md section 6.9, which a recomputation from the variant list does not.

secondary.label: Recomputed from variants, pivot contigs >= 5 kb only
secondary.rationale: Every published reference number in this file is FILTERED: SKA2 restricts itself to the shared k-mer core, and the mapping pipeline drops high-depth and low-identity regions (32 raw SNPs -> 2 filtered for isolate-A-isolate-B). Infinity-Win deliberately does not filter (PROJECT.md section 2 lists no filtering among its goals; section 15 says repeats are flagged, not corrected). Comparing unfiltered output against filtered references is therefore not apples to apples, so the same comparison is also run on a filtered basis: variants on pivot contigs shorter than 5 kb are dropped. The contig length is read from the contig name (e.g. isolate-B_contig37_len1448_cov139.5).
secondary.provenance: docs/REAL_DATA_VALIDATION.md - the extra differences between isolate-A and isolate-B all sit on one 1,448 bp pivot contig at 139.5x coverage, about 3.4x the chromosomal depth, i.e. a high-copy element that every reference pipeline excludes.
secondary.caveat: This is a recomputation by the benchmark scripts, not an engine output. It counts positions where two members' alleles differ and does NOT apply the comparable-coverage restriction of section 6.9, so its unfiltered value can exceed the engine's own. Treat it as evidence about the filter, never as a replacement for the engine's distance.

pairs.name: isolate-A-isolate-B
pairs.source: SKA2 (split k-mer, alignment-free) distance on fastp-trimmed reads

provenance.analysis: ska build/ska distance on the read sets listed in analysis/ncbi_pd/ska/reads.tsv
provenance.cross_check: The same pair is recorded as 2.0 in analysis/results.json under ska_reads['isolate-A|isolate-B'], and as filtered_snps=2 (from raw_all_snps=37, unique_snps=32) in the assembly pairwise section of the same file.

pairs.name: isolate-A-isolate-C
pairs.source: SKA2 (split k-mer, alignment-free) distance on fastp-trimmed reads

provenance.analysis: ska build/ska distance on the read sets listed in analysis/ncbi_pd/ska/reads.tsv
provenance.cross_check: The same pair is recorded as 2.0 in analysis/results.json under ska_reads['isolate-A|isolate-C'], and as filtered_snps=2 (from raw_all_snps=17, unique_snps=16) in the assembly pairwise section of the same file.

pairs.name: isolate-B-isolate-C
pairs.source: Reference mapping followed by SNP filtering

provenance.analysis: Reads mapped to a reference, variants called and then filtered; the filtered count is what is recorded. The unfiltered call for this pair was 21 raw / 17 unique SNPs, all of which the filter removed.
provenance.cross_check: SKA2 independently reports Distance 0.00 for this pair (mismatch count 22 over 4671404 matched split k-mers) in analysis/ncbi_pd/ska/cluster_reads_distance.tsv, and analysis/results.json ska_reads['isolate-B|isolate-C'] is 0.0.

how_to_use.observed_from: Infinity-Win's cluster_<id>.dist.tsv SNP counts in the run output folder, joined by genome name; if a bench JSON carries pairwise errors it is used as a cross-check
how_to_use.verdict_rule: PASS when |observed - expected| <= abs_tolerance_snps for all three pairs; 'not measured' (never PASS) when Infinity-Win reports no distance for a pair, because the three isolates were not placed in one cluster

caveats: The expected values are READ- and MAPPING-based; Infinity-Win works on the ASSEMBLIES in bench-work/salmonella_trio/asm/. A disagreement of one SNP is evidence about the assemblies, not automatically a bug.
With three taxa no tree accuracy can be measured (Robinson-Foulds needs at least four), so this dataset contributes distance accuracy only.
If isolate-B and isolate-C are 0 SNPs apart they may be collapsed into one profile group; Infinity-Win must still report a distance of 0 for that pair rather than omitting it.
